expectations.text: Produces a Job Story that frames the problem from the affected user's perspective
expectations.evidence: Job Story: 'When I am using the candles API during normal operations, I want the system to enforce per-client request limits, so that a single abusive or misconfigured client cannot degrade response times and availability for everyone else.' Frames from the affected user's perspective.

expectations.text: Produces a Promise with specific, measurable guarantees (e.g., request limits, response times)
expectations.evidence: Promise includes: 'per-client rate limit based on the client's tier (free or paid)', 'clear 429 response with rate limit metadata', 'Other clients' request latency and availability are unaffected'. Specific and measurable.

expectations.text: Adds Acceptance Criteria the user didn't explicitly mention (edge cases like what happens when limit is hit, rate limit headers, etc.)
expectations.evidence: Added: fail-open if Redis unavailable, rate limit headers (X-RateLimit-Limit/Remaining/Reset), 5ms p99 latency constraint, configurable via env vars, specific example numbers (60/600 req/min), isolation between clients.

expectations.text: Treats Redis mention as context/constraint rather than prescribing the solution
expectations.evidence: Redis in Constraints: 'Must use the existing Redis instance for rate limit counters (no new infrastructure)' and Context: 'Redis is already running in the infrastructure'. Not prescribed as the solution in the Job Story.

expectations.text: Addresses the tier-based limits (free vs paid) in the acceptance criteria
expectations.evidence: AC #2: 'Free-tier clients have a configurable request limit (e.g., 60 requests/minute)' and AC #3: 'Paid-tier clients have a separate, higher configurable request limit (e.g., 600 requests/minute)'. Even includes concrete example values.

expectations.text: Presents the complete draft for user confirmation
expectations.evidence: Presents draft and asks 4 specific questions: client identification method, specific limit numbers, fail-open vs fail-closed preference, endpoint exemptions.

expectations.text: Shows the acorn issue create command with --label ready-for-spec
expectations.evidence: Shows: acorn issue create candles "Add tiered API rate limiting to protect service quality" --label ready-for-spec --body "$(cat <<'EOF'...EOF)" with full issue body.
